issues.legal_issue: Charges that a tenant expressly agrees to pay as part of the rent are recoverable as rent through distress proceedings.
material_facts: The tenancy agreement required the tenants to pay municipal taxes and electricity charges as part of the rent.
The landlord sought to recover municipal taxes through a distress warrant.
issues.conclusion: The tenants could not contend that the agreed municipal taxes and electricity charges were not rent recoverable by distress warrant.
issues.legal_principle: The express terms of the tenancy made the municipal taxes and electricity charges part of the rent; the Court applied section 53 of the Presidency Small Cause Courts Act, 1882, which provides for recovery by distress warrant. No earlier cases were cited on this issue.

predicates.distress_recovery_proceeding: A landlord sought to recover an amount from a tenant through a distress proceeding.
predicates.tenancy_terms_make_charges_part_of_rent: The tenant agreed in the tenancy terms to pay the disputed charges as part of the rent.
predicates.agreed_charges_are_recoverable_as_rent_b: The agreed charges may be recovered as rent through distress.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks recovery by distress and the tenant agreed that the charges form part of the rent, those charges are recoverable as rent by distress.

issues.legal_issue: A procedural rule made within the authority conferred by the governing rent-control law does not become invalid merely because jurisdiction is later reorganized or adapted.
material_facts: The State Government made Rule 5 under the authority to prescribe procedure for rent-control proceedings, including execution of decrees and distress warrants.
Following reorganization and the enactment of legislation governing the successor jurisdiction, the rule continued in force and applied to the court hearing the dispute.
The appellants did not show that the rule had become ultra vires in its application to the successor jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: Rule 5 was not ultra vires and continued to apply to the relevant court.
issues.legal_principle: Section 49(2)(iii) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947 authorized rules prescribing procedure, including procedure for execution and distress warrants. Rule 5 was made under that authority. It continued in force under section 87 of the Bombay Reorganization Act, 1960, and the Court found no showing that it became ultra vires after the Ahmedabad City Courts Act, 1961. No earlier cases were cited on this issue.

rule.if: delegated_rule_challenge and rule_made_within_express_rulemaking_power and rule_continued_for_successor_jurisdiction and no_conflict_shown_after_adaptation

predicates.delegated_rule_challenge: A party challenged the validity of a procedural rule made by the government under authority conferred by legislation.
predicates.rule_made_within_express_rulemaking_powe: The government made the rule within the authority given to prescribe procedure for the relevant proceedings.
predicates.rule_continued_for_successor_jurisdictio: The rule continued to apply to the jurisdiction after a legal reorganization or adaptation.
predicates.no_conflict_shown_after_adaptation: The challenger did not show that the rule conflicted with the law as adapted for the successor jurisdiction.
predicates.delegated_procedure_rule_is_valid: The delegated procedural rule remains valid and applicable.

issues.definition: If a challenged procedural rule was authorized, continued to apply after reorganization, and was not shown to conflict with the adapted law, the rule remains valid and applicable.

issues.legal_issue: A court with exclusive jurisdiction over rent-control disputes retains the powers conferred on it by the law governing that court, including the power to issue distress warrants.
material_facts: The Ahmedabad court was an existing Small Causes Court governed by the Presidency Small Cause Courts Act, 1882.
Legislation gave that court exclusive jurisdiction over suits and proceedings arising under the rent-control law.
The governing court law expressly empowered courts governed by it to issue distress warrants, and the relevant procedural rule applied to the proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The court had power to issue a distress warrant in a proceeding within its exclusive rent-control jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28 of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947 gave designated existing courts exclusive jurisdiction over the specified disputes; it did not create a special court stripped of the powers conferred by the law governing it. Sections 17 and 18 and the Schedule to the Ahmedabad City Courts Act, 1961, applied the Presidency Small Cause Courts Act, 1882, in the relevant jurisdiction and amended the rent-control law to designate the court. Section 53 of the Presidency Small Cause Courts Act conferred the power to issue distress warrants, and Rule 5 prescribed the applicable procedure. No earlier cases were cited on this issue.

predicates.rent_control_proceeding: A suit or proceeding concerns rights or obligations arising under rent-control law.
predicates.existing_court_given_exclusive_subject_m: Legislation gives an existing court exclusive jurisdiction over the relevant category of disputes.
predicates.governing_court_law_authorizes_distress_: The law governing that court empowers it to issue distress warrants.
predicates.procedure_rule_applies_to_proceeding: A procedural rule applicable to the proceeding provides for the procedure the court is to follow.
predicates.court_may_issue_distress_warrant: The court may issue a distress warrant in the proceeding.

issues.definition: In a rent-control proceeding, an existing court with exclusive jurisdiction may issue a distress warrant when the law governing it grants that power and the applicable procedural rule governs the proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: The pendency of an application to determine standard rent does not bar a distress warrant for amounts due under the applicable rent or payment order when the landlord cannot access amounts deposited in court.
material_facts: The tenants applied to have standard rent determined, and the court fixed the contractual rent as interim standard rent and ordered payment of rent and municipal taxes.
The tenants deposited the municipal taxes in court, but the court did not permit the landlord to withdraw that deposit.
The municipal taxes remained due and payable by the tenants, and the landlord could not use the deposit to pay them.
issues.conclusion: The pending standard-rent application did not suspend the power to issue a distress warrant, and the municipal taxes were in arrears because the landlord could not access the deposit.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 11 of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, a court may determine standard rent and interim standard rent. Until standard rent is determined or an interim order is made, the contractual rate remains payable; the Court held that the pending application does not itself suspend recovery by distress. Under section 53 of the Presidency Small Cause Courts Act, 1882, distress could be sought for amounts in arrears. A deposit that the landlord could not withdraw did not make the amount available to the landlord or prevent it from being in arrears. No earlier cases were cited on this issue.

predicates.rent_standard_fixing_proceeding: A tenant has a pending proceeding to determine standard rent, including an interim rent determination.
predicates.amount_remains_due_under_applicable_paym: The tenant remains liable for an amount under the rent or payment order applicable in the proceeding.
predicates.landlord_cannot_access_deposited_amount: An amount deposited in court is not available for withdrawal by the landlord.
predicates.distress_warrant_available_for_unpaid_ar: A distress warrant may be issued to recover the amount that remains in arrears.

issues.definition: When a rent-standard proceeding is pending, an amount remains due under the applicable payment order, and the landlord cannot access a court deposit, distress remains available for the unpaid arrears.
